Proposed solution: BLUPRINT v1

Design / Wireframes / Layout options05

Three layouts, sketched

Crazy-8-style layout sketches before any detail. Two of them were built and tested.

A · SaaS dashboard

Sidebar, dark theme, dense panels. Familiar from analytics tools.

B · Store page

Announcement bar, store header, campaign hero, product-style tiles. BLUORNG's own language.

C · Card feed

Instagram-like grid of insight cards. Fast to scan, weak for comparing numbers.

Round 1 pick
A, the SaaS dashboard

Chosen first because it felt like a 'real tool' to the team.

Round 2 pick
B, the store page

After usability round 1: the team wanted it to feel like BLUORNG, not like software.

Dropped
C, the card feed

Hard to compare numbers side by side; tables and bars won.

TakeawayLayout A was tested first; testing pushed the design to B. The usability section shows why.

Design / Paper prototype10

Paper prototype kit (reference)

A kit for making and testing a paper version by hand before building.

Sheets to draw (A4 landscape)

1 · Header + tabs + hero
2 · KPIs + top 10
3 · What's working
4 · Avoid + hashtags
5 · Posting heatmap
6 · Ideas (4 cards)
7 · Calendar
8 · Mobile: 4 phone frames

Cut-outs

Tooltip · active tab underline · 'Reel' filter state · CSV saved toast · hover outline · 3 confidence tags

Materials

Black marker, grey marker, red pen for warnings, sticky notes for tooltips, scissors, a phone-size card.

How to run it

One facilitator plays the computer and swaps sheets; one notes. Use tasks T1 to T3. 10 minutes per person.

Visual design / Design system12

Design system: principles

Four principles and a three-level token structure behind every screen.

01
A store, not software

Use BLUORNG's store patterns: announcement bar, store header, campaign hero, product tiles.

02
Evidence first

Every claim shows its number: '+25% vs average', '51 of 1,394 comments'.

03
Black is good, red is a warning

Monochrome by default. Red only for below-average results and things to avoid.

04
Big type, few words

Wide uppercase headings carry the page; body text stays short and plain.

Primitives#0b0b0b, #f4f4f4, #c3141b, 4-pt spacing, Archivo, Geist
→
Semantic tokens--ink, --muted, --heat, --bg-2, --display, --body
→
ComponentsButton, tab, tag, KPI tile, idea card, bar row, heat cell
TakeawayTokens let the same system make the dashboard, the deck and the next screens consistent.

Visual design / UI elements / Icons15

Icons and brand marks

A deliberately small icon set: five functional icons and five glyphs.

Functional icons · 24 px grid, 1.75 stroke, square ends

downloadExport CSV
printPrint
externalOpen post
arrowPrimary CTA
sortSortable column

Glyphs and legend keys

✦tickerSeparator in the announcement bar
×lockupBG × BLUPRINT
legend: lineRolling average
legend: dotOne post
legend: squareBars, cells, tags
Rule

Text first, like the BLUORNG store: icons appear only on utility actions (export, print, open post, CTA). Navigation stays text-only.

Brand marks

BG monogram in the header, BLUORNG wordmark in the hero background and footer, 3D BG mark as the campaign image.

TakeawayFewer icons keep the store feel; each one that exists marks an action.

Visual design / UI elements / Components18

UI elements: charts and tables

Data components, each with a value printed next to the mark.

Bar rowsLabel + count, bar on white track, value + lift. Black / grey / red by lift.
Heat cellsAverage and post count; dashed when empty.
Hashtag cloudSize = uses, colour = performance.
Calendar rowInk rule + confidence badge on idea rows.

Style guide

The rules that keep new screens consistent: space, shape, motion and words.

TokenValueUse
Space4 · 8 · 14 · 18 · 22 · 28 · 36 · 56 · 96 pxGaps 14, panel padding 18–26, section 56–96
Container1320 px max, 16–40 px side marginAll sections
Corners0Everything is sharp, like the store
Borders1 px #dcdcdc · 2 px ink or redDividers · emphasis rules
ElevationNoneFlat surfaces; contrast does the work
Motioncubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1), 120–300 msHover, press (scale .97), tab underline

Numbers+25% vs average1.25x baseline
Big numbers33.8k33,826
Ideas“It's back. For 48 hours.”Restock communication post
ConfidenceHigh confidence0.82
Dates30 Oct, Fri2026-10-30
TakeawayShort words and sharp edges: the same discipline BLUORNG's store uses.
Visual design / Interaction patterns20

Interaction patterns

How the dashboard responds, documented so every new control behaves the same way.

TooltipHover or keyboard focus. Value first, then context. Follows the pointer.
Sticky header + active tabTabs stay on top; the current section is underlined; a 2 px line shows scroll progress.
Filter chipsOne choice at a time; rows hide instantly; 'All' resets.
PatternTriggerFeedback
Open postClick a top-10 barOpens Instagram in a new tab
Sort tableClick a column headerRows reorder, click again to reverse
ExportExport CSVDownloads instagram-audit-posts.csv
PressAny buttonScales to 97%, 160 ms
Reduced motionOS settingTicker and smooth scroll stop
TakeawayEvery hover has a keyboard twin, and every motion has a reduced-motion fallback.

Accessibility checks (WCAG 2.2, iOS, Android)

Contrast ratios computed from the real colour tokens; layout checked at 320, 390 and 1440 px.

CheckBeforeAfterStatus
1.4.3 Text contrast (AA)Muted text on panels 4.25:1 (#747474)4.85:1 (#6b6b6b)Fixed
1.4.11 Non-text contrastNear-average bars 2.35:1 (#a9a9a9)3.45:1 (#8a8a8a)Fixed
1.4.3 One-off hashtags1.42:1 (#cfcfcf)4.85:1, lighter weightFixed
1.4.1 Use of colourColour + value labels, legendsSamePass
1.4.10 Reflow at 320 px25 px sideways scrollNo page scroll; tables scroll insideFixed
2.5.8 Target size / iOS 44 pt / Android 48 dpButtons and chips 32–40 px44 px tallFixed (iOS) · Partial (Android)
2.4.7 Focus visible2 px outline on every controlSamePass
1.3.1 Headings, tablesReal h1–h4, th headersSamePass
2.2.2 Pause moving contentTicker pauses on hover, stops with reduced motionSamePass

TakeawaySix issues found and fixed in the dashboard itself. Android's 48 dp target is the one partial pass.
Source: WCAG 2.2, Apple HIG, Material Design

Prototype and test / Digital prototype26

Digital prototype

Instead of a click-through mock-up, the prototype is the product running on test data.

bluprint / @bluorng
Built as
A working HTML prototype

One self-contained file: no install, opens on any laptop or phone, works offline.

Real pipeline
Apify → analysis → page

The prototype runs on the same code that will run on the real scrape.

Interactive
Hover, filter, sort, export

Tooltips, sticky tabs, calendar filter, sortable table, CSV export, print.

Test data
Clearly labelled

Prototype and test / Usability evaluation / Plan27

Usability test plan

What we tested, with whom, and how success was measured.

Method
Moderated, think-aloud

In person at the BLUORNG office, on the team's own laptops and phones. 25–30 minutes each.

Participants
6 per round, 2 rounds

Marketing lead, performance marketer, social media manager, content strategist, photographer, co-founder.

Metrics
Success · time · errors · SEQ · SUS

SEQ after each task (1–7), SUS at the end (0–100).

Rounds
R1: version 1 (dark) · R2: version 2

Same tasks, same people, two weeks apart.

#TaskSuccess when
T1Find the best-performing format and how much better it doesNames Reels and +25%
T2Name two hashtags BLUORNG should stop usingAny two from the Stop list
T3Find the best day and time to postFri, prime time (19–22)
T4Pick a high-confidence idea and say why it should workCites the data signal
T5Find the next Reel in the calendarCorrect date within 60 s
T6Export the post data for a reportCSV downloaded
TakeawayThe six tasks come straight from the task flows, so the test checks the jobs the design was made for.

Heuristic evaluation

An expert review against Nielsen's 10 heuristics, before and after the redesign.

Worst severity found per heuristic (0 none · 4 catastrophe)

Heuristic (Nielsen)Version 1Version 2
Visibility of system status20
Match with the real world30
User control and freedom11
Consistency and standards20
Error prevention11
Recognition rather than recall21
Flexibility and efficiency11
Aesthetic and minimalist design30
Help users recover from errors00
Help and documentation21
Biggest v1 issue
Didn't match BLUORNG

Dark SaaS look and blue/orange colours read as a generic tool, not the brand (match with the real world, aesthetics).

Status
Where am I?

v1 sidebar disappeared on phones. v2 adds sticky tabs, an active underline and a progress line.

Documentation
What is 'engagement'?

v2 defines it in the section intro and footer.

TakeawayThe redesign removed every severity-3 issue. What's left are minor (1) issues.
Source: Expert review, 2 reviewers

Heuristic review

What works
  • Opening the page and knowing the state of the account in under 30 seconds.
  • Ideas that say why: participants quoted the data back when choosing.
  • Looks like BLUORNG: the co-founder approved sharing it in the planning meeting.
Next
  • Version 2: Meta ads results and the Ad Library next to organic data (goals G2, G5).
  • Claude AI write-ups for each idea, plus a shoot planner (G4).
  • Monthly live refresh from the real scrape; test again with real BLUORNG data.
TakeawayVersion 2 of the design meets the usability bar. The next step is real data and the ads layer.

The final solution: BLUPRINT

A content audit and planning dashboard for BLUORNG, in BLUORNG's own visual language.

bluprint / @bluorng
GoalStatus
